subject: physics
title: Wave properties and the wave equation
key_idea: A wave is described by its **amplitude**, **wavelength**, **frequency** and **period**. Wave speed is found from **v = f × λ**, or from distance ÷ time. The period is 1 ÷ the frequency.

blocks.text: These words describe any wave. Learn each meaning exactly.

items.meaning: The maximum displacement of a point on a wave away from its undisturbed position.
The distance from a point on one wave to the equivalent point on the adjacent wave.
The number of waves passing a point each second. It is measured in hertz, Hz.
The time taken for one complete wave to pass a point.
The speed at which energy is transferred, or the wave moves, through the medium.
A line joining points on a wave that are at the same stage, such as all the peaks.

items: Amplitude is measured from the undisturbed position to a peak, not from a trough to a peak.
Wavelength can be measured from peak to peak, or trough to trough.
1 Hz is one wave per second.
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the undisturbed position.
Wavelength is the distance between equivalent points on adjacent waves.
Frequency is the number of waves passing a point each second.

blocks.text: Frequency and period are linked. A high frequency means a short period.

blocks.label: Period
where: period, T, is in seconds, s
frequency, f, is in hertz, Hz

items: A wave of frequency 5000 Hz has a period of 1 ÷ 5000 = 0.0002 s.
Change kilohertz to hertz first. 8.0 kHz = 8000 Hz.
Change gigahertz to hertz first. 1 GHz = 1 000 000 000 Hz.
Period = 1 ÷ frequency.
Convert kHz and GHz to Hz before you calculate.

blocks.text: All waves obey the wave equation. It links wave speed, frequency and wavelength.

blocks.label: Wave equation
blocks.formula: wave speed = frequency × wavelength   (v = f λ)
where: wave speed, v, is in metres per second, m/s
frequency, f, is in hertz, Hz
wavelength, λ, is in metres, m

blocks.label: Wave speed from distance and time
blocks.formula: wave speed = distance ÷ time   (v = x ÷ t)
where: wave speed, v, is in metres per second, m/s
distance, x, is in metres, m
time, t, is in seconds, s

items.text: Put every quantity in m/s, Hz and m. For example, 4.5 km/s = 4500 m/s.
Write the equation with the numbers in it.
To find the wavelength, divide the wave speed by the frequency.
State m, Hz or m/s with the answer.

blocks.text: A sound wave has a frequency of 220 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 330 m/s. Calculate the wavelength.

diagram.alt: Calculate a wave speed from a frequency and a wavelength.
diagram.question: A water wave in a ripple tank has a frequency of {f} Hz and a wavelength of {l} m. Calculate the wave speed.

blocks.text: Try the slider. It shows water ripples with a wave speed of 0.25 m/s. Change the frequency and the amplitude.

diagram.alt: Change the frequency and amplitude of water ripples travelling at 0.25 m/s to see the wavelength and period.

items: Wave speed stays the same, so a higher frequency gives a shorter wavelength.
The amplitude does not change the wavelength, the frequency or the period.
v = f × λ, with the speed in m/s, the frequency in Hz and the wavelength in m.
Rearrange before you substitute, or substitute and then rearrange. Show both steps.
Convert km/s, kHz, GHz and nm to m/s, Hz and m first.

blocks.text: The speed of a wave is found by measuring its frequency and wavelength, or by timing it over a distance.

items.text: Place a metre rule at the side of the screen, perpendicular to the wavefronts. Measure the length of several waves and divide by the number of waves.
Count the number of waves that pass a given point. Time them with a stop clock and divide the number of waves by the time.
Calculate the wave speed using v = f × λ.

blocks.text: The speed of sound in air

items: Make a sound, such as a hammer hitting a metal plate.
Two microphones connected to an electronic timer measure the time for the sound to travel between them.
Repeat the measurement several times and take a mean time.
Calculate speed = distance between the microphones ÷ mean time.

blocks.text: (Separate science) When a sound wave passes into another medium, its frequency stays the same. Its speed and wavelength change together, because v = f λ. If the speed increases, the wavelength increases.

items: Measure the wavelength and the frequency of ripples, then use v = f λ.
Time a sound over a known distance, repeat and take a mean.

checks.q: Describe what is meant by the wavelength of a wave.
checks.a: The distance from a point on one wave to the equivalent point on the adjacent wave.

checks.q: A wave has a frequency of 2.5 Hz. Calculate its period.

worked_example.question:
An S-wave has a frequency of 3.6 Hz. The S-wave has a speed of 4.5 km/s.

Calculate the wavelength of this S-wave.

Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
worked_example.tip: A correct substitution or rearrangement with an unconverted speed can still score marks. An answer of 1300 m is also allowed.

blocks.text: Make observations to identify the suitability of apparatus to measure the frequency, wavelength and speed of waves in a ripple tank and waves in a solid, and take appropriate measurements.

worked_example.question:
In a swimming pool, a wave is produced with a wavelength of 4.0 m and a velocity of 0.8 m / s.

Calculate the frequency of the wave.

State the unit of frequency.

Use the equation

v = f × λ
answer_points: unit: Hz (or s⁻¹, or per second)
worked_example.tip: The unit is an independent mark, so it can be scored even if the calculation is wrong.

extra.heading: Echoes and the distance to an object

items: A pulse that reflects from an object travels there and back.
Use distance = speed × time for the whole journey, then divide by 2.

worked_example.question:
A musician plays a guitar.

This makes a sound wave in the air.

The frequency of the sound wave is 440 Hz.

The speed of sound is 330 m / s.

Calculate the wavelength of the sound wave.

Use the equation: wave speed = frequency × wavelength
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 0.75 m scores 3 marks. A correct substitution into the given equation scores 1 mark.

worked_example.question:
A sound of frequency 13 kHz is transmitted through water.
The speed of sound in water is 1500 m / s.
Calculate the wavelength of this sound in water.
answer_points: Write the equation: v = f × λ, so λ = v ÷ f.
Change the frequency to hertz: 13 kHz = 13 000 Hz.
λ = 0.115 m, which is 0.12 m to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the equation, one for the substitution and one for the answer.

blocks.text: Two more words describe the shape of a wave, and a sound wave has two properties you hear.

items.meaning: The highest point of a wave.
The lowest point of a wave.

items: A larger amplitude makes a louder sound.
A higher frequency makes a higher pitch.

worked_example.question:
Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) uses radio waves to detect changes in material underground.

GPR radio waves have a frequency of 170 MHz.

The speed of radio waves is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

Calculate the wavelength of the waves.
answer_points: Change the frequency to hertz: 170 MHz = 170 000 000 Hz.
Write the equation: λ = v ÷ f.
worked_example.tip: One mark is lost if the frequency is not converted to hertz.

blocks.text: The pitch of a sound depends on the frequency of the vibrating source.

items: A source vibrating at a higher frequency makes a higher pitch.
A source vibrating at a lower frequency makes a lower pitch.
